papers.title: Antitumor potentials of matrine; molecular and cellular mechanisms and interactions with immune cells in the tumor microenvironment.
papers.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
papers.authors: Charoghdoozi K, Dehnavi S, Sadeghi M, Bazrafshani S, Mohammadi M
papers.abstract:
Cancer continues to be the second leading cause of death globally and poses a significant public health issue. There is growing research and clinical interest in natural compounds that possess strong anticancer properties. Matrine, a quinolizidine alkaloid sourced from the traditional Chinese herbal remedy Sophora flavescens, shows a wide array of pharmacological actions, including antitumor, anti-inflammatory, antiviral, antiarrhythmic, hepatoprotective, antibacterial, and analgesic effects.
This summary outlines the antitumor mechanisms of matrine, focusing on its interactions with immune cells in the tumor microenvironment. It also covers matrine's chemical properties, challenges in clinical translation, and future research directions.
This study conducted a narrative review using searches across the PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases. The primary keywords included matrine, its structural class, and its antitumor and immunomodulatory mechanisms. The literature reviewed spanned from 2001 to 2026.
Matrine has shown a range of drug-related effects., encompassing properties such as antitumor, anti-inflammatory, antiviral, antiarrhythmic, and hepatoprotective, antibacterial, and analgesic properties. Recent research has indicated that matrine exhibits potential anti-cancer properties via various molecular mechanisms, including the capacity to suppress the growth of cancer cells, trigger cell cycle arrest, stimulate the death of cancer cells, hinder angiogenesis, prevention of cancer invasion and metastasis, overcome multidrug resistance, lessen or prevent the harmful effects linked to chemotherapy or radiotherapy when used in combination with different chemotherapeutic drugs, and also exert anticancer effects through its interaction with immune cells. Structure-activity data point to the D-ring lactam as a key determinant of bioactivity, while nanoparticle-based delivery and combination regimens appear promising for addressing matrine's pharmacokinetic limitations. Clinical evidence, however, remains limited.
Matrine is a multi-target natural compound and may have direct antitumor and immunomodulatory capabilities. Existing preclinical studies have identified that matrine is a promising candidate for cancer therapy development. Independent validation of mechanisms, chemical optimization, and specific delivery technology, along with human pharmacokinetic and safety studies, are all key to applying matrine for clinical treatment.

papers.title: Beyond sleep macrostructure: a high-definition review of acupuncture's electrophysiological signatures in modulating sleep microarchitecture (spectral power, spindles, and slow oscillations).
papers.authors: Fu F, Huang Y
papers.abstract: Sleep science has shifted from coarse stage-based metrics toward a microstructural perspective that treats electroencephalographic biomarkers, spectral power, sleep spindles, and slow oscillations as candidate windows onto restorative brain function. This high-definition review evaluates whether acupuncture has been shown to modify these features. Direct evidence from natural overnight sleep is currently very limited: most available electrophysiological studies were conducted during quiet wakefulness, in resting daytime EEG recordings from clinical groups, or under propofol anesthesia. These studies demonstrate that acupuncture or related electrical acupoint stimulation can produce state-, region-, and frequency-dependent changes in EEG power and network organization, but they do not yet establish increased NREM spindle density, improved slow-oscillation-spindle coupling, enhanced slow-wave morphology, memory consolidation, or glymphatic clearance. We therefore distinguish directly observed findings from indirect mechanistic support and from hypotheses that require prospective testing. Plausible pathways include ascending somatosensory influences on thalamocortical excitability, autonomic and hypothalamic effects that may reduce hyperarousal, and peripheral or central neurochemical processes involving adenosine, GABA, serotonin, and BDNF; however, the causal sequence from needling to sleep microarchitecture remains unproven. Future progress requires preregistered, adequately powered, multi-night studies using validated spindle and slow-wave detectors, explicit control estimands, and multimodal measurements. Biomarker-guided and closed-loop acupuncture should presently be regarded as a research framework rather than an established treatment strategy.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture inhibits the nuclear factor kappa B signaling pathway and alleviates knee synovial membrane inflammation and chondrocyte apoptosis in a rat model of knee osteoarthritis.
papers.journal: Acupuncture in medicine : journal of the British Medical Acupuncture Society
papers.authors: Lu M, Meng DH, Li T, Luan GR, Luo SY, Liu CB et al.
papers.abstract:
Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a degenerative joint disease that is characterized by cartilage degeneration and inflammation. According to reports, electroacupuncture (EA) can delay joint cartilage degeneration and inhibit inflammation, but its specific mechanisms remain unclear. The objective of this study was to examine the mechanisms through which EA potentially improves cartilage degeneration and inhibits inflammation in KOA.
In this study, we used monosodium iodoacetate injections to establish a rat KOA model and then performed EA. Cartilage morphology and chondrocyte apoptosis were assessed by hematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining, transmission electron microscopy and scanning electron microscopy. Levels of inflammatory mediators in the synovial membrane were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Expression of apoptotic factors in cartilage was analyzed by reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and Western blotting. Nuclear factor (NF)-κB pathway components were evaluated by immunofluorescence. To validate the mechanistic role of NFκB signaling, KOA rats were transfected with a NFκB-overexpressing lentivirus, and the effects of EA on phosphorylated (p)-p65, p-IκBα (inhibitor of NFκB), synovial inflammatory factors and cartilage apoptotic markers were examined.
HE staining, transmission electron microscopy and scanning electron microscopy showed that EA alleviated chondrocyte apoptosis in our rat model of KOA. ELISA results showed that EA significantly inhibited the expression of inflammatory factors (tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, matrix metalloproteinase (MMP)-13, and interleukin (IL)-6) and promoted the expression of the anti-inflammatory factor IL-10 in the synovial membrane. RT-qPCR and Western blotting results showed that EA significantly decreased the expression of apoptotic factors, including the B-cell lymphoma (Bcl-2)-associated X protein (Bax)/Bcl-2 ratio, caspase-3, caspase-8 and caspase-9 in cartilage. Immunofluorescence results showed that EA regulated the NFκB inhibitor protein IκBα and inhibited NFκB p65. In addition, after KOA rats were transfected with an overexpressing NFκB lentivirus, p-p65 expression was significantly upregulated, p-IκBα expression was significantly decreased, and the expression of pro-inflammatory factors in the synovial membrane and apoptosis-related factors in cartilage were significantly upregulated. After EA, p-p65 expression was significantly decreased, p-IκBα expression was significantly upregulated, and the expression of pro-inflammatory factors in the synovial membrane and apoptosis-related factors in cartilage decreased.
EA decreased synovial inflammation and chondrocyte apoptosis, thereby alleviating cartilage degeneration in a rat model of KOA. EA reversed NFκB signaling pathway activation after NFκB lentivirus transfection, showing that inhibition of synovial inflammation and chondrocyte apoptosis and alleviation of cartilage degeneration by EA are associated with inhibition of NFκB signaling pathway activation.

papers.title: Acupotomy for myofascial pain syndrome: What to report and why.
papers.journal: Acupuncture in medicine : journal of the British Medical Acupuncture Society
papers.authors: Zhang W, Yuan K, Luo R, Pan L, Jiang Y, Kong D
papers.abstract:
Several needling-based procedures, including acupotomy, are used for myofascial pain syndrome. Established reporting guidance covers many aspects of acupuncture and other non-pharmacological interventions, but acupotomy reports may still omit procedural details needed for replication.
To identify procedure-specific details that may improve reporting of acupotomy for myofascial pain syndrome and clarify how these details relate to established reporting guidance.
Using a non-systematic descriptive approach, we compared selected acupotomy procedural reports with STRICTA, TIDieR, CONSORT NPT, CONSORT 2025 and CONSORT Harms. Procedure-specific details requiring greater acupotomy-specific description were organized into five domains: targeting, access, layer, release and endpoint. We then applied these domains to a published randomized trial of ultrasound-guided acupotomy as a worked example. This organization is intended to make procedural variation explicit; it is not presented as a validated checklist or minimum reporting set. General intervention information remains covered by existing guidance. Harms reporting should reflect anatomical and procedural context, and outcome assessment should prioritize patient-important outcomes such as pain and region-appropriate function. Imaging used to guide the procedure should be reported according to its role, whereas imaging- or physiology-based outcome measures are better treated as exploratory or mechanistic when relevant.
Clearer procedural reporting may make acupotomy studies easier to reproduce, compare and synthesize. The five domains are preliminary and require empirical testing and stakeholder input.

papers.title: Deep Vein Thrombosis Complicated by the Dissemination of Muscular Tuberculosis due to Acupuncture Treatment.
papers.authors: Chen S, Lai Y, Liang R
papers.abstract: ObjectivesTo present a rare case of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the right upper extremity caused by muscular tuberculosis (MTB), likely disseminated via acupuncture, and to describe the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges encountered.MethodsThis case report details the clinical presentation, diagnostic workup, and management of a patient with MTB-associated DVT. The patient was treated with standard anti-tuberculosis therapy (rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol) along with anticoagulation therapy (low-molecular-weight heparin and rivaroxaban). Surgical intervention (debridement and drainage) was required due to abscess formation during treatment.ResultsInitially, the patient's DVT had an unclear etiology but was ultimately attributed to MTB. Despite complications including tuberculous abscess formation, combined medical and surgical management led to a successful outcome with resolution of infection and thrombosis.ConclusionsMuscular tuberculosis, though rare, should be considered in cases of unexplained DVT, particularly in patients with risk factors such as invasive procedures (eg, acupuncture). Early diagnosis, combined anti-TB therapy, anticoagulation, and surgical intervention, when necessary, can lead to favorable outcomes.

papers.title: MAGR-TCM: a knowledge graph-powered multi-agent model for intelligent home health consultation and triage in TCM gynecology.
papers.authors: Lv M, Pan X, Li Y, Hu Y, Xu W, Jin L et al.
papers.abstract:
Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) demonstrates distinct efficacy in managing gynecological disorders. However, accessing this specialized care in a home setting remains challenging due to the high cost of frequent hospital visits, privacy concerns, and a lack of immediate professional guidance. While general-purpose artificial intelligence offers a convenient alternative, the semantic gap between a patient's colloquial symptom descriptions and formal TCM diagnostic logic-compounded by the inherent 'hallucination' risks of large language models-prevents these tools from providing safe, actionable advice. To bridge this gap, this study proposes MAGR-TCM, an intelligent home health consultation and triage model.
Under expert supervision, a domain-specific knowledge graph was constructed, encompassing 10,231 entities and 32,051 relationships extracted from 741 high-quality clinical case records. Based on this foundation, we developed a Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework comprising four specialized agents designed to reconstruct the complete TCM 'Disease-Pattern-Therapeutic Principle-Formula-Medicinal' reasoning chain from informal user inquiries. This collaborative architecture simulates the expert diagnostic process to generate logical, evidence-based health guidance.
Experimental results demonstrate that MAGR-TCM significantly outperforms all baseline models on both RAGAS automatic evaluation and expert human evaluation. The model achieved 100% sensitivity and specificity on the safety test set, further validating its practical utility in home health settings and its ability to distinguish self-treatable conditions from those requiring urgent hospital care.
By transitioning from black-box predictions to transparent, safe, and explainable reasoning logic, MAGR-TCM offers a technological paradigm for patient-centered home health management. It effectively mitigates generative hallucinations, making professional TCM expertise safely accessible for women's daily self-care and preliminary triage.

papers.title: Barriers to Complementary and Integrative Health Use Among Veterans on Long-Term Opioid Therapy.
papers.journal: Journal of integrative and complementary medicine
papers.authors: Kazemitabar M, Kerns RD, Becker WC, Heapy AA, Abel EA, Rajeevan H et al.
papers.abstract:
Complementary and integrative health (CIH) therapies are increasingly promoted within the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) as nonpharmacologic approaches and adjuncts to long-term opioid therapy (LTOT) for chronic pain. However, uptake remains modest, and barriers to initiation and continuation are poorly understood.
We conducted a cross-sectional survey of 126 Veterans with chronic pain on LTOT who had no CIH utilization documented in VHA electronic health records between July 1, 2017, and December 31, 2022. Participants were sampled from a national VHA cohort of over 280,000 Veterans. Respondents reported familiarity with nine CIH services-acupuncture, biofeedback, guided imagery, clinical hypnosis, therapeutic massage, meditation, tai chi/qi gong, yoga, and chiropractic care-as well as prior use and reasons for non-use or discontinuation. Barriers were summarized overall and stratified by age, sex, and race.
Fewer than 10% of Veterans reported regular use of most modalities, with chiropractic care as the exception (23% regular use). Common reasons for non-use included lack of knowledge about eligibility, uncertainty about how to begin, and skepticism about effectiveness. Discontinuation was most often attributed to perceived ineffectiveness, cost, and logistical challenges. Younger Veterans more frequently reported not knowing they were eligible or how to start, while White Veterans more often cited doubts about effectiveness, and Black Veterans reported discomfort with particular modalities. Self-practice therapies (yoga and meditation) were more commonly practiced at home; whereas hands-on therapies (acupuncture, chiropractic care, and massage) were largely accessed in community settings where cost and logistics were prominent barriers.
Substantial barriers remain to CIH service engagement among Veterans on LTOT, spanning awareness, logistics, and personal comfort. Targeted education, streamlined referrals, and strategies to manage early expectations may improve uptake and sustainment.

papers.title: Oxytocinergic neurons in the paraventricular nucleus mediate the analgesic effect of electroacupuncture in inflammatory pain.
papers.authors: Liu J, Wang X, Han Q, Chen Y, Zheng B, Yang W et al.
papers.abstract:
Electroacupuncture (EA) is a well-established and effective analgesic intervention, particularly for inflammatory pain; however, the analgesic effect of EA is closely related to the stimulation frequency, amplitude, and acupoint. The underlying neural mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify the central neural projections responsible for EA-induced analgesia and to investigate the mechanisms underlying its frequency-specific effects.
In this study, we utilized a mouse model of carrageenan (CGN)-induced inflammatory pain to explore the analgesic effects of EA. In vivo fiber photometry and immunofluorescence were employed to monitor the activity of oxytocinergic neurons in the paraventricular nucleus (PVN). The role of neuronal activity in EA-induced analgesia was assessed through chemogenetic and pharmacological approaches.
We demonstrated that specific activation of PVN oxytocinergic neurons significantly alleviated pain behaviors in the inflammatory pain model mice. EA stimulation of the Stomach meridian 36 (ST36) activated PVN oxytocinergic neurons and exerted an antinociceptive effect in a frequency-dependent manner. Specifically, lower frequency EA stimulation induced more significant PVN oxytocinergic neuronal activity and analgesic effect, while higher frequency EA stimulation did not show significant neuronal activation or pain relief. Chemogenetic silencing of PVN oxytocinergic neurons completely abolished EA-induced analgesia. Additionally, we identified that oxytocinergic projections from the PVN to the arcuate nucleus (ARC) were activated only under lower frequency EA stimulation, while higher frequency EA stimulation failed to exert this effect. What's more, locally blocking the target of oxytocin in the ARC significantly attenuated the analgesic effect of EA.
Our findings highlight the critical role of PVN oxytocinergic neurons in mediating the frequency-specific analgesic effects of EA, which provide important evidence for parameter selection in clinical EA treatment for pain.

summary.clinical_takeaway: 이 연구는 염증성 통증에서 전침의 효과가 자극 주파수에 따라 달라질 수 있으며, PVN 옥시토신성 경로가 관련될 가능성을 시사한다.

papers.title: Quassin attenuates secondary brain injury following intracerebral hemorrhage.
papers.authors: Mazhar M, Bizhanova A, Muhammad A, Siddique R, Zhang R, Qi L et al.
papers.abstract:
Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) accounts for only 10-15% of all stroke cases, yet it is responsible for up to 70% of stroke-related mortality and long-term disability globally. Quassin, a white, crystalline molecule, is often used in Chinese herbal medicine. Research has shown quassin's neuroprotective properties associated with the inhibition of neuroinflammation in neurological diseases.
A total of 120 C57BL/6 male mice were randomly divided into three groups of 40: the Sham group, the ICH + Vehicle group, and the ICH+ Quassin group. ICH was induced in the two experimental groups by injecting collagenase type VII into the basal ganglia. The ICH + quassin group received daily intraperitoneal administration of quassin (1 mg/kg) for three consecutive days. Neurological function was assessed using both the corner test and mNSS. Three days post-ICH, several analyses were conducted: TUNEL staining, Western blot, Evans Blue dye extravasation, and Immunofluorescence/Immunohistochemistry staining were utilized to evaluate molecular targets, blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, and cellular responses.
Quassin treatment significantly improved neurological recovery and exerted a robust protective capacity against acute structural secondary injury, achieving a 72.5% reduction in total lesion volume compared to vehicle controls (p < 0.0001). Quassin markedly suppressed neuroinflammation, as evidenced by a significant decrease in Iba-1+ microglial activation (p < 0.0001) and neutrophil infiltration (p < 0.001). Moreover, quassin treatment was correlated with the downregulation of the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling pathway (p < 0.01) and a notable reduction in pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-α and IL-6. Furthermore, quassin attenuated neuronal apoptosis (p < 0.0001) and preserved BBB structural integrity by suppressing MMP-9 expression (p < 0.01) while upregulating key tight junction proteins, including zonula occludens-1 (p < 0.0001) and Occludin (p < 0.001).
Quassin demonstrates significant neuroprotective efficacy in mouse models of ICH by concurrently reducing neuroinflammation, preserving the integrity of the BBB, and mitigating brain cell death.

papers.title: A novel ratiometric molecularly imprinted electrochemical microsensor with synergistic embedded signal and surface reference probes for non-electroactive Aβ42 detection.
papers.authors: Yu Z, Kong X, Chen X, Huang M, Tang D, Ye Z et al.
papers.abstract: Ratiometric molecularly imprinted electrochemical sensors (RMIESs) can mitigate electroactive surface area effects, background interference, and signal fluctuations while enhancing anti-interference capability and stability, but reported sensors are mainly suitable for electroactive targets. Herein, a novel RMIES strategy using an acupuncture needle (AN) was demonstrated for the non-electroactive biomarker β-amyloid1-42 (Aβ42). On the AN, an acid chrome blue K-electropolymerized imprinted layer serves as the recognition unit, embedded hemin acts as the Aβ42-modulated signal probe, and surface caffeic acid (CA) serves as the internal reference, forming a common-interface ratiometric system. CA was employed for the first time as an electroactive internal reference probe. The hemin-CA peak potential difference is 600 mV in differential pulse voltammetry, sufficient for ratiometric electroanalysis. This ratiometric microsensor exhibits a wide linear detection range (0.1 ∼ 5 × 106 pg/mL) and a low detection limit (0.0104 pg/mL) for Aβ42. Compared with the single-signal built-in sensor, it shows superior detection performance, anti-interference capability, and reproducibility. Furthermore, an AN-based microelectrode electrochemical system was explored and used on pig brain tissue. This microsensor provides a novel ratiometric electroanalysis strategy for non-electroactive biomarkers and is suitable for integration because it avoids external mediators, enables miniaturization, and allows multifunctional integration with acupuncture.

papers.title: Integrative therapies for symptom management in dementia from a palliative perspective: narrative review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
papers.authors: Nixdorff N, Montagnini M, Lee PG
papers.abstract:
Dementia affects over 55 million people worldwide, with behavioral and psychological symptoms (BPSD) impacting over 90% of individuals. Conventional pharmacotherapies offer limited benefits with substantial side effects. Integrative care therapies (ICT) represent a complementary approach, yet the evidence supporting their use has been largely absent from the palliative care literature. This narrative review synthesizes ICT systematic reviews and meta-analyses to bridge this gap.
PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO, and the Cochrane Library were searched for systematic reviews and meta-analyses published between 2015 and June 2026 evaluating ICT for dementia symptom management. Seminal earlier works were also included when updated reviews were unavailable. Individual randomized controlled trials (RCTs), validation studies, and non-English publications were excluded, except selected sources cited for mechanistic, safety, regulatory, or pivotal-trial context.
Cognitive stimulation achieved the highest evidence certainty, with high-certainty evidence for communication and social interaction and moderate-certainty evidence for cognition, quality of life (QOL), and challenging behaviors. Music therapy showed moderate-certainty evidence for depression improvement but not agitation. Light therapy and movement-based mind-body therapies (MBT) demonstrated benefit across the broadest range of domains-including cognition, BPSD, and sleep-though certainty remained low-to-very-low. Massage and aromatherapy showed consistent short-term benefits for agitation and depression. Acupuncture augmented conventional medication for improvement in cognition and activities of daily living (ADL). Dietary and herbal therapies contributed primarily to cognitive domains, with Ginkgo biloba showing the most robust BPSD evidence. Cannabinoids showed preliminary evidence for agitation and in severe disease. Across modalities, effects were often limited to the treatment period, early-stage disease showed the most robust benefits, and safety profiles were favorable. Only cognitive stimulation and music therapy achieved moderate or higher Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) ratings.
Multiple ICT modalities show promising evidence for dementia symptom management that aligns with palliative care principles, though most evidence is of low-to-very-low certainty. Future research should prioritize pragmatic trials in hospice and palliative care settings using outcomes meaningful to this context, including comfort, caregiver experience, and healthcare utilization.

papers.title: The STAT3/JAK2 Signaling Pathway in Renal Fibrosis: Mechanistic Insights and Advances in Targeted Intervention.
papers.authors: Yu Y, Lv J, Chai Y, Wang X, Yu M
papers.abstract: Renal fibrosis remains a major therapeutic challenge in chronic kidney disease. Evidence for therapies targeting signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) is predominantly preclinical, although Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors have been evaluated in diabetic kidney disease. This review compares STAT3 signaling across acute kidney injury progressing to chronic disease, diabetes, hypertension, and hyperuricemic kidney injury. Cytokine receptors, growth-factor receptors, metabolic stress, and interorgan signals influence STAT3 activity in tubular, stromal, and immune cells. Their effects depend on cellular context, activation dynamics, and interactions with other fibrotic pathways. We distinguish pathway-associated changes from functional validation and direct target engagement when assessing synthetic inhibitors, cell-based therapies, and natural or traditional-medicine-derived interventions. Clinical albuminuria findings are considered separately from evidence of fibrosis regression. Priorities include cell-resolved pharmacodynamic markers, intervention windows defined by repair state, and evaluation of targeted delivery.

papers.title: Differences in cytotoxicity and apparent extracellular glucose utilisation among sequentially prepared Cinnamomum cassia stem-bark extracts in basal and palmitate-associated C2C12 myotubes.
papers.authors: Shikwambana H, Mapfumari NS, Makhubela S, Madihlaba M, Mokgotho P, Shai LJ et al.
papers.abstract:
Cinnamomum cassia bark has a documented history of use in traditional medicine and food-medicine practices associated with diabetes and metabolic disorders. This study compared preliminary phytochemical fingerprints, MTT metabolic-viability responses and apparent extracellular glucose utilisation among sequentially prepared stem-bark extracts.
Authenticated, vouchered stem bark was extracted sequentially with n-hexane, ethyl acetate, ethanol and water. Extracts were examined by thin-layer chromatography and qualitative phytochemical screening. MTT reduction was assessed after 72 h. Residual extracellular glucose was measured after 180 min, and apparent extracellular glucose utilisation was calculated as 15 mmol/L minus the residual concentration. This endpoint does not directly measure membrane glucose transport or intracellular utilisation. Three independent experiments were conducted in technical triplicate, with technical wells averaged within experiments. The retained non-insulin basal well-level values were reconstructed from reported summary statistics and were therefore treated descriptively; the palmitate-associated dataset was analysed using independent-experiment means.
The sequential fractions showed different preliminary fingerprints and concentration-related MTT profiles. Within each palmitate-associated extract series, one or more concentrations showed greater apparent extracellular glucose utilisation than the concurrent palmitate-only control; no formal comparison among extracts was performed.
Sequential fractions showed different MTT and apparent extracellular glucose-utilisation profiles. The endpoint is indirect, was not normalised to concurrent viability or cell number, and may be affected by vehicle or assay interference. Quantitative cinnamaldehyde and coumarin characterisation was not performed. The findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish glucose uptake, GLUT4 activation, insulin sensitisation, extract superiority, therapeutic efficacy or in vivo safety.
papers.title_ko: C2C12 근관에서 계피(Cinnamomum cassia) 줄기껍질 연속 추출물의 세포독성과 세포외 포도당 이용의 차이

summary.question: 연속적으로 제조한 계피 줄기껍질 추출물들이 C2C12 근관에서 세포독성과 외부 포도당 이용 양상에 차이가 있는지 평가했다.

papers.title: Safety and Effectiveness of Motherwort Injection for Hemostasis and Menstrual Regulation: Protocol for a Prospective, Observational, Multicenter Real-World Study.
papers.authors: Wang S, Li M, Guan S, Liu J, Dang H, Wang Z et al.
papers.abstract:
Motherwort injection (MI) is a traditional Chinese medicine injection widely used for hemostasis and menstrual regulation in obstetrics and gynecology. Although clinical trials and systematic reviews have demonstrated its effectiveness for specific indications, comprehensive real-world evidence (RWE) regarding its safety, effectiveness, and use patterns across diverse clinical settings remains limited.
This study aims to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of MI in routine clinical practice and to generate RWE to support its rational use in women receiving treatment for approved obstetric and gynecological indications.
This prospective, observational, multicenter real-world registry study plans to enroll 20,000 patients receiving MI for approved obstetric and gynecological indications in routine clinical practice in China. Treatment decisions, including whether to use MI and the dose and duration of treatment, as well as the use of concomitant medications, are made independently by treating physicians. Safety outcomes include the occurrence, type, severity, and incidence of adverse events and adverse drug reactions (ADRs). Effectiveness outcomes are assessed according to the clinical indication and include perioperative bleeding, postpartum hemorrhage, postabortion bleeding and menstrual resumption, uterine involution, menstrual regulation, and treatment satisfaction. Descriptive statistics will be used to characterize patient characteristics, MI use, and safety and effectiveness outcomes. Prespecified subgroup analyses will examine heterogeneity across major clinical groups. An exploratory nested case-control analysis with 1:4 matching and conditional logistic regression will be used to investigate factors associated with the occurrence of ADRs.
This study has received funding and obtained ethics approval in March 2024 (approval P24003-PJ03). Participant recruitment began on March 31, 2026. By September 2026, a total of 774 participants had been enrolled and included in the study database. The protocol specifies a target sample size of 20,000 participants, with data collection, monitoring, and quality control being conducted according to standardized study procedures. Data analysis has not yet commenced, and the study findings are expected to be published in October 2027.
This study will provide large-scale RWE regarding the safety and effectiveness of MI in obstetric and gynecological practice. The findings are expected to support postmarketing safety surveillance, optimize clinical decision-making, and contribute to the evidence-based evaluation of traditional Chinese medicine injections.

papers.title: Phytochemistry and multi-target pharmacological mechanisms of Abelmoschus manihot (L.) Medicus in diabetic nephropathy.
papers.authors: Zhu W, Su F, Zhao M, Tian M, Tang L
papers.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy is a leading cause of end-stage renal disease, but current therapies remain limited in efficacy and safety. Abelmoschus manihot (L.) Medicus possess kidney protecting effects in traditional Chinese medicine. Modern clinical practice has used its standard preparation Huangkui capsules to treat kidney diseases and confirmed flavonoids are main active ingredients. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the phytochemical profile of A. manihot, with emphasis on flavonoids, and systematically summarises their multi-target pharmacological mechanisms in DN, including anti-inflammatory, anti-oxidant, anti-fibrosis and cytoprotective effects. Additionally, the structural characteristics of the compounds also describe in this article, providing a chemical rationale for the development of flavonoid-based therapeutics against this complex disease.

papers.title: Structure-based isolation of bioactive Strychnos indole and new aporphine alkaloids from traditional Chinese medicine as anti-MRSA candidates: computational screening and antibacterial evaluation.
papers.authors: Khattab OM, Yosri N, Liu Q, Zhou Z, Han J, Ling Z et al.
papers.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) harbours structurally diverse alkaloids with potential against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Here, 983 alkaloids from 82 TCM species were screened by multi-target molecular docking against four MRSA resistance proteins, among them IleRS, PBP2a, DNA gyrase, and PBP2a-penicillin G acyl-enzyme, prioritising 50 top-ranked candidates (ΔG ≤ -7 kcal/mol). Bisindole strychnines from Strychnos nux-vomica were top-ranked leads, confirmed by 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations. Feature-based molecular networking (FBMN) via GNPS2 directed bioassay-guided isolation from S. nux-vomica and Aristolochia contorta, yielding 24 alkaloids including two new aporphines, 2,4-dihydroxy-1-methoxynoraporphine (N2) and 2,4-dihydroxy-1-methoxyaporphine (N3), fully characterised by 1D/2D NMR and HRESIMS. Antibacterial evaluation against S. aureus ATCC6538 and MRSA ATCC BAA-1717 revealed the lipophilic noraporphines asimilobine (N4) and 1,2-dimethoxynoraporphine (N5) as the most potent compounds, with MIC50 values against MRSA of 16.5 ± 7.1 and 11.3 ± 9.8 µg/mL, respectively (191 µg/mL and inactive, respectively, against MSSA). Structure-activity analysis identified lipophilic methoxylated noraporphine scaffolds and the bisindole strychnine skeleton as key pharmacophoric features, identifying these alkaloids as candidate anti-MRSA leads warranting further in vivo validation.

papers.title: Acupuncture after surgery of soft tissue tumors of the extremities: postoperative pain and feasibility: a prospective trial.
papers.authors: Ghanad E, Fischer H, Weiß C, Dusch M, Menge F, Weigl H et al.
papers.abstract:
Acute pain management following resection of soft tissue tumors (STTs) of the extremities is primarily based on pharmacological interventions. However, current guidelines emphasize the role of complementary non-pharmacological approaches, such as acupuncture. This prospective pilot study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and potential effects of acupuncture following STT surgery of the extremities. Furthermore, this study represents the first to systematically assess the postoperative pain trajectory in this patient population.
In this prospective, single-arm, single-centre study, 25 patients undergoing surgical resection of STTs of the extremities received acupuncture on postoperative day (POD) 1. Pain intensity was recorded at predefined time points using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) and the Brief Pain Inventory (BPI).
Participants had a mean age of 60.7 years. Most tumors were malignant, located in the lower extremities, with a median size of 13.1 cm. Postoperative pain at rest was minimal, with a mean NRS score of 1.2 (± 1.2) on POD 1 and below 0.5 (± 0.8) from POD 2 onward. The pain severity index of the BPI declined significantly after POD 1, reaching its lowest level at POD 3. Acupuncture was administered on POD 1. Placement of needles at the "optimal position" was feasible in 8 of 25 patients. The median length of hospital stay was four days. Wound complications occurred in eleven patients, but none were attributable to acupuncture. No other serious adverse events were observed.
Acupuncture was feasible, safe, and well accepted in this postoperative setting. Pain levels and opioid requirements remained low throughout the postoperative period. Further controlled studies are warranted to assess efficacy and to refine patient selection and acupuncture techniques in this setting.

papers.title: A Novel sMRMHR Pseudotargeted Method for Rapid Chemome Comparison Among Herbal Medicines: from Metabolome to Exposome.
papers.authors: Wang X, Shen CX, Shao SM, Ma TB, Cui J, Ren QX et al.
papers.abstract: The metabolomic comparison of closely related herbal species, both the intrinsic plant metabolome and the subsequent in vivo exposome, is vital for ensuring drug safety and elucidating therapeutic mechanisms. However, such a comparison is challenging because medicinal plants within the same genus share similar chemical profiles with minor chemical or abundance differences, and their in vivo exposure levels are typically low and are affected by complex biological matrices. In this study, Curcumae Radix (CR), a traditional Chinese medicine derived from the roots of four Curcuma species, was used as a case study. A pseudotargeted workflow based on scheduled high-resolution multiple reaction monitoring (sMRMHR) was established to compare the metabolites and plasma exposure profiles of these species, using a transition library constructed from the four plant species. The sMRMHR pseudotargeted method showed acceptable linearity, repeatability, and stability in QC samples and 12 reference standards, with performance comparable to that of SWATH and TOF MS1 while maintaining stable coefficients of variation (CVs) at low concentrations. Specifically, 95.2% of metabolomic features showed linearity with R2 ≥ 0.8, 98.16% showed a CV ≤ 30%. In exposomics, 83.14% of exposures had matrix effect factor (MF) CVs below 30%, and over 300 exposures showed MFs within 70%-130%. Finally, the application results of CR demonstrate its capability for chemome comparison of metabolites and exposures. In conclusion, this approach provides a practical HRMS-based strategy for the integrated comparison of plant metabolite profiles and plasma exposure-related profiles across closely related medicinal species, and may support subsequent studies of interspecies chemical differences and in vivo exposure characteristics after oral administration.

papers.title: Identification and resistance characterization of two traditional Chinese medicine plant species against Meloidogyne incognita.
papers.authors: Pan S, Wei P, Zhao M, Liu C, Sun Z, Bai J et al.
papers.abstract:
Root-knot nematodes are major plant pests responsible for global agricultural losses. However, systematic studies on host suitability of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) plants for Meloidogyne species remain limited, leaving their resistance status unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the suitability of TCM plants as hosts for Meloidogyne incognita and characterize their resistance modes, with a single microplot trial providing supporting evidence.
Of the 25 TCM species evaluated for host suitability for M. incognita, 23 were susceptible based on the reproduction factor. Taraxacum mongolicum developed root galls but produced no egg masses and was thus classified as highly resistant, whereas Plantago asiatica produced neither galls nor egg masses and was considered non-host. Although T. mongolicum supported high initial nematode penetration, nematode development was arrested, and the nematode population declined over time. In P. asiatica, significantly fewer penetrated nematodes, arrested development, and population reduction were observed. The number of root galls formed in T. mongolicum was comparable to that on susceptible hosts, but the galls were significantly smaller, with histological observations revealing inhibited giant cell formation. A single microplot trial provided supporting evidence that both T. mongolicum and P. asiatica reduced M. incognita populations in naturally infested soil compared to susceptible hosts.
T. mongolicum was highly resistant and P. asiatica was a non-host to M. incognita, as both suppressed nematode development and reproduction. These species may be suitable for rotation with other susceptible medicinal crops to reduce M. incognita populations, providing a potential management strategy. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

papers.title: A function-guided multi-omics integrated strategy to reveal the effective chemicalome and mechanisms of the 50% ethanol extract of Eucommia ulmoides leaf in alleviating osteoarthritis.
papers.authors: Xu KX, Sun S, Leng HX, Zheng KF, Xin GZ, Shi ZQ
papers.abstract: Conventional multi-omics integration in herbal medicine research relies mainly on statistical correlations and pathway analyses, potentially overlooking key bioactive metabolites and their associated enzyme targets. To address this, we developed an enzyme function-guided strategy integrating chemomics, metabolomics, and microbiomics to reveal the potential mechanism of the 50% ethanol extract of Eucommia ulmoides leaf (EEUL) against osteoarthritis (OA). The anti-inflammatory, cartilage-repairing, and analgesic effects of EEUL were confirmed in zebrafish phenotypic screening models and in the mouse OA model induced by the high-cholesterol diet (HCD) combined with anterior cruciate ligament transection (ACLT). Integrated metabolomic and microbiomic analyses further showed that OA-associated metabolic dysregulation and gut microbial dysbiosis were significantly reversed by EEUL. Remarkably, gut microbiota-derived bile salt hydrolase (BSH) was prioritized by enzyme function-guided analysis as a functional bridge linking the EEUL chemicalome to the altered metabolome. Meanwhile, the bioactive chemical constituents of EEUL, such as quercetin and kaempferol, exhibited high binding affinity to BSH. Consistently, BSH activity was reduced and the bile acid pool was modified by EEUL, accompanied by decreased intestinal farnesoid X receptor (FXR) expression, increased circulating glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) levels, and upregulated articular GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R) expression. Collectively, these findings suggest that the ameliorative effect of EEUL on osteoarthritis may be mediated via the putative gut FXR-joint GLP-1R axis. By establishing enzyme-level functional connections among multi-omics, this study provides a novel framework for elucidating the mechanisms of herbal medicine and explores a promising strategy for developing long-term and safe OA interventions.

papers.title: Naofucong mitigates amyloid-β deposition and cognitive deficits by enhancing insulin-degrading enzyme expression and inhibiting BACE through MAPK pathway inhibition.
papers.authors: Tian Y, Ma M, Yin R, Jing G, Zhang M
papers.abstract: Amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation is a key pathological event in cognitive disorders. While the traditional Chinese medicine Naofucong has shown neuroprotective potential, its precise effects on Aβ metabolism remain unclear. This study investigated whether Naofucong modulates Aβ pathology by regulating key enzymes involved in its production and degradation. We employed Aβ-overexpressing 293-APP-BACE cells and treated them with Naofucong-containing serum. To further investigate the involvement of the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathway, the MAPK pathway inhibitor Trans-Zeatin (TZ) was used as a mechanistic reference tool to explore the involvement of MAPK signaling. This pharmacological inhibition approach was used to support the involvement of MAPK signaling in mediating the effects of Naofucong. Expression levels of insulin-degrading enzyme (IDE), amyloid precursor protein (APP), β-site APP cleaving enzyme (BACE), and Aβ were measured. In addition, the activation status of MAPK signaling (ERK, JNK, p38) was assessed. Naofucong-containing serum significantly upregulated IDE expression and downregulated APP and BACE levels, leading to reduced intracellular and extracellular Aβ accumulation. Furthermore, Naofucong suppressed excessive phosphorylation of ERK, JNK, and p38 in the MAPK pathway, an effect that was consistent with that observed following TZ intervention. These findings suggest that Naofucong mitigates Aβ deposition, at least in part, by enhancing IDE-associated Aβ degradation and suppressing BACE-associated Aβ production. This dual regulatory effect may be associated with inhibition of the MAPK signaling pathway, as supported by pharmacological blockade using TZ, highlighting a multi-target mechanism of Naofucong in Aβ-associated cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Comparative effectiveness of non-pharmacological interventions on postoperative kinesiophobia in total knee arthroplasty: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.authors: Xie M, Yang Y, Shi H, Wu S, Chen S, Wang W et al.
papers.abstract:
Kinesiophobia can hinder recovery after total knee arthroplasty (TKA); however, the comparative effectiveness of various non-pharmacological interventions remains unclear. Through this network meta-analysis (NMA), we aimed to compare and rank these interventions for reducing postoperative kinesiophobia.
Eight databases were searched from inception to July 20, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating non-pharmacological interventions for kinesiophobia after TKA were included. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Random-effects pairwise meta-analysis and frequentist NMA were performed using standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Certainty of evidence was assessed using Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation for pairwise comparisons and Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis for the NMA.
71 RCTs involving 6776 participants were included, comprising 13 network nodes. Ten interventions significantly reduced kinesiophobia compared with usual care. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) showed a significant effect versus usual care (SMD = -2.42, 95% CI: -3.07 to -1.78) and ranked highest according to SUCRA (81.9%), followed by psychological interventions (77.3%), multidisciplinary team interventions (76.8%), and traditional Chinese medicine nursing (73.3%). The certainty of evidence was generally low or very low.
Current evidence suggests potential benefits of several non-pharmacological interventions, particularly CBT; however, confidence in comparative effects and rankings is limited by risk of bias, small-study effects, heterogeneity, and limited direct comparisons.
Not applicable.
The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251036979).

papers.title: Mechanism of Sini Decoction and its self-assembled component in improving Doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy.
papers.authors: Liu Y, Pu Z, Chen X, Peng Y, Peng C, Li X
papers.abstract:
Sini decoction (SND) is a typical Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) prescription composed of Aconitum carmichaelii Debx, Zingiberis Rhizoma, and Glycyrrhizae Radix et Rhizoma Praeparate cum Melle, used to treat cardiomyopathy in TCM clinical trials. Recent studies have shown that the active ingredients of SND can form self-assembled complexes during decoction, whose bioactivity differs from that of the monomeric compound. However, current research on the active ingredients of SND has not yet included these self-assembled components, and the mechanism by which SND exerts its effects on doxorubicin (Dox)-induced cardiomyopathy remains unclear.
This study aimed to investigate the underlying mechanisms by which SND and its self-assembled component (SAC) improve Dox-induced cardiomyopathy in mice. The complete isolation of the self-assembled complex component from SND was achieved for the first time, and its activity and mechanism were explored, providing a new perspective for revealing the substance basis of TCM prescriptions.
SAC and the unassembled component (SMC) were separated from SND by ultrafiltration, and UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS was used to qualitatively analyze their chemical components. Based on the main components of SAC, Benzoylmesaconine-glycyrrhizic acid complex (GBMA) was prepared under simulated decoction conditions of SND. A mouse model of cardiomyopathy was established by intraperitoneal injection of Dox, followed by oral administration of SND, SAC, SMC, and GBMA, to evaluate improvements in cardiac systolic function across treatment groups. The effects of SND and its components on cardiac systolic function were evaluated to reveal the differences in their medicinal effects. The mechanisms by which SND and SAC improve cardiomyopathy were systematically investigated using Seahorse energy metabolism analysis, autophagic flux analysis, and Western blotting, with a focus on the interconnected organelles, mitochondria, and autophagosomes.
A total of 173 compounds were identified in SAC. Among them, molecules with lower hydrophilicity tend to self-assemble in the decoction, while molecules with a molecular weight less than 300 Da participate less in self-assembly. SND, SAC, and GBMA significantly improved abnormal cardiac systolic function in Dox-induced cardiomyopathy mice, while SMC had no such effects. SAC and GBMA inhibited Dox-induced excessive mitophagy by downregulating BNIP3 and MFN2 expression, thereby protecting mitochondria and cardiomyocyte nuclei. SND, SAC, and GBMA all alleviated mitochondrial functional impairment in the cardiomyopathy model. They could trigger energy metabolism reprogramming (reducing the expression of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex subunits PDC-E2 and PDC-E3, and increasing the expression of OXPHOS-CI and OXPHOS-CIV) to optimize mitochondrial energy supply efficiency. SMC could downregulate CII expression in OXPHOS and exert some mitochondrial protective effects, but failed to significantly improve mitochondrial functional impairment.
SND and SAC administration improve Dox-induced cardiomyopathy. They could protect mitochondria and cardiomyocyte nuclei through optimizing mitochondrial energy metabolism efficiency and inhibiting autophagy, while the specific active constituents and their absorption routes remain to be determined. This study elucidates the molecular mechanism by which the adminstration of SAC in SND improves Dox-induced cardiomyopathy, providing new scientific evidence for the combined clinical application of SND and Dox. It also offers a new approach to the research of the substance basis of TCM prescriptions, namely, focusing on the self-assembled substances present in the decoction, rather than assuming the active components are small molecules, to accurately reveal the overall effects of TCM prescriptions and the scientific connotation of their compatibility. It should be noted that the current findings are based on a single batch of SND, and further validation using multiple batches is required to confirm the consistency of the observed effects.

papers.title: Traditional Chinese medicine interventions for hyperhomocysteinemia-associated vascular injury: an evidence-mapped, mitochondria-centered review.
papers.authors: Xie H, Zhang W, Wang Y, Sun Z, Bai M, Xiao J et al.
papers.abstract:
Hyperhomocysteinemia (HHcy) is associated with vascular injury. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) has an ethnopharmacological background in vascular disorders, and contemporary evidence warrants focused evaluation in HHcy-associated vascular injury.
To integrate clinical and experimental TCM evidence, distinguish direct HHcy/Hcy evidence from supportive evidence, and map mechanistic relationships and evidence boundaries.
This structured narrative review with evidence mapping searched PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, and CNKI Academic Journals through October 13, 2026, and classified evidence according to intervention identity and HHcy directness. Formal study-level risk-of-bias assessment was not completed for the final human evidence set.
The review identified 71 scientifically distinct intervention-level entities: 9 extracts/fractions, 27 isolated compounds, 14 formulas/herb pairs, 16 patent/marketed medicines, 3 combination regimens, and 2 derivatives/salts. The final direct-evidence set comprised 199 independent direct studies, including 84 human, 45 animal, and 70 directly relevant experimental studies. Mechanistic findings were synthesized qualitatively across recurring vascular and mitochondrial themes; quantitative network topology was not reported because independently verified edge-level provenance was not established.
TCM interventions show broad mechanistic evidence relevant to HHcy-associated vascular injury, but the qualitative evidence map reflects mechanistic coverage rather than therapeutic efficacy. Evidence remains predominantly experimental/preclinical, and evidence for durable cardiovascular or cerebrovascular benefit remains insufficient. Further work requires standardized interventions, rigorous mechanistic validation, and well-designed clinical studies assessing long-term safety and vascular outcomes.

papers.title: Catalpol alleviates glandular and pulmonary injury in primary Sjögren's syndrome via regulation of sphingolipid metabolism.
papers.authors: Cui T, Luo J, Li Z
papers.abstract:
In traditional Chinese medicine, pSS-related oral and ocular dryness is associated with depletion of yin and body fluids, while pulmonary involvement may reflect impaired lung moistening. Rehmannia glutinosa is traditionally used to nourish yin, generate fluids, and relieve dryness. Catalpol, its major iridoid glycoside, may provide a pharmacological basis for these traditional uses.
This study investigated the protective effects of catalpol in experimental pSS and examined the involvement of KDSR-mediated sphingolipid metabolism.
An antigen-induced experimental Sjögren's syndrome (ESS) mouse model, interferon-γ-stimulated A253 cells, and transforming growth factor-β-stimulated NIH-3T3 fibroblasts were used. Pseudo-targeted sphingolipidomics, multi-cohort transcriptomic analysis, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, cellular thermal shift assays, and KDSR knockdown were performed.
Catalpol improved salivary secretion and reduced glandular inflammation and epithelial apoptosis in ESS mice. It also attenuated ESS-associated pulmonary inflammation and fibrosis-related changes and suppressed fibroblast activation. Integrated sphingolipidomic and transcriptomic analyses identified disease-associated KDSR upregulation and alterations in the sphinganine/3-ketodihydrosphingosine ratio. Molecular simulation and cellular thermal shift assays supported a potential interaction between catalpol and KDSR. Catalpol reduced KDSR expression and inhibited integrin/FAK/MYH9 signaling, whereas KDSR knockdown attenuated its protective effects in vitro.
Catalpol ameliorated glandular dysfunction and pulmonary injury in experimental pSS. These effects were associated with KDSR-mediated sphingolipid metabolism and suppression of integrin/FAK/MYH9 signaling.

summary.question: 캇탈폴이 실험적 원발성 쇼그렌증후군에서 샘 기능저하와 폐 손상을 완화하는지, 그리고 그 기전이 KDSR 매개 스핑고지질 대사와 관련되는지 평가했다.

summary.clinical_takeaway: Rehmannia glutinosa 유래 캇탈폴은 실험적 pSS에서 건조증과 폐 침범과 관련한 병태를 완화할 가능성을 보여 한약 본초의 기전 연구 근거가 될 수 있다.

papers.title: Adaptogens in Stress-Related Disorders: Scientific and Pharmacological Review.
papers.journal: Central nervous system agents in medicinal chemistry
papers.authors: Rathod H, Patel A, Patel D, Chandarana C
papers.abstract:
Stress-related disorders have become a major global health concern, contributing substantially to psychological, metabolic, and neurodegenerative conditions. Adaptogenic herbs, traditionally used in Ayurvedic, Chinese, Korean, and Indigenous medical systems, have gained scientific interest because of their potential to enhance stress resilience, normalize physiological functions, and modulate neuroendocrine responses. These botanicals exert multitarget effects, including regulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, antioxidant activity, and modulation of key neurotransmitters. A growing body of evidence highlights the potential of adaptogens such as Withania somnifera, Rhodiola rosea, Panax ginseng, Bacopa monnieri, and others to alleviate psychological stress, enhance cognitive performance, and support metabolic balance.
Major adaptogenic herbs were evaluated by examining preclinical, molecular, and clinical literature related to stress physiology. Relevant databases were searched for studies reporting effects on glucocorticoids, HPA-axis biomarkers, oxidative stress pathways, neurotransmitter balance, immune modulation, and subjective psychological stress outcomes. Historical and ethnomedicinal sources were also reviewed to contextualize traditional uses.
Evidence indicates that adaptogens may regulate the HPA axis by modulating CRH, ACTH, and cortisol levels; enhance cellular protection by inducing heat shock protein 70 (Hsp70); and activate antioxidant pathways, including the Nrf2 pathway. Several adaptogenic herbs exhibit anxiolyticand antidepressant-like effects through modulation of GABA, serotonin, and dopamine signaling. They may also reduce inflammatory markers, improve mitochondrial energy metabolism, and mitigate cognitive fatigue. Clinical findings suggest potential improvements in mild-to-moderate anxiety, perceived stress, cognitive performance, and fatigue, although the strength of evidence varies among individual adaptogens and study designs.
Adaptogens differ from conventional anxiolytics and antidepressants in that they are proposed to exert broad, systems-level regulatory effects rather than acting primarily on a single pharmacological target. Their pleiotropic neuroendocrine, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and cytoprotective actions may support their therapeutic potential in chronic stress and related conditions. However, direct comparisons with established pharmacotherapies remain limited, and claims regarding dependence, withdrawal, and comparative safety require cautious interpretation. Traditional uses are increasingly being examined through molecular and clinical research.
Adaptogenic herbs represent a promising class of natural agents with the potential to enhance stress tolerance, support physiological homeostasis, and exert neuroprotective and metabolic effects. Their multitarget mechanisms and reported clinical benefits support continued investigation of their use as complementary interventions for stress-related disorders. Larger, well-designed, standardized clinical trials are required to establish efficacy, optimal dosing, long-term safety, and clinically relevant herb-drug interactions.

papers.title: Acute idiopathic blind spot enlargement syndrome in a patient with high myopia: A case report with multimodal imaging findings.
papers.authors: Liu H, Liu Z, Wu Q, Yang Y, Pan X
papers.abstract:
To report the clinical manifestations, multimodal imaging features, and treatment outcomes of a case of acute idiopathic blind spot enlargement syndrome (AIBSES) in a patient with high myopia.
A 47-year-old male with high myopia presented with sudden visual field (VF) obscuration and photopsia in the left eye, with best-corrected visual acuity of 0.05 in the affected eye at initial examination.
Based on characteristic VF findings showing diffuse central sensitivity depression with a temporal defect contiguous with the physiological blind spot, optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing heterogeneous reflectivity of the neurosensory retina and focal discontinuity of the ellipsoid zone (EZ) signal, and multifocal electroretinography demonstrating reduced P1 response amplitude density across all 5 tested rings, a diagnosis of AIBSES was established.
The patient received systemic corticosteroid therapy, followed by additional pharmacologic treatment and adjunctive acupuncture at the 4-month follow-up.
At the 7‑month follow‑up, best-corrected visual acuity improved from 0.05 to 0.2, with substantial improvement in the VF defect and gradual restoration of EZ continuity on OCT. Because spontaneous recovery is recognized in AIBSES, the observed improvement cannot be attributed solely to corticosteroid therapy.
AIBSES is an outer retinopathy characterized by acute VF defects, photopsia, and outer retinal structural abnormalities, with visual dysfunction that may be disproportionate to relatively subtle fundoscopic findings. Characteristic VF defects and EZ disruption on OCT are important diagnostic features. AIBSES should be considered in patients presenting with acute visual decline or VF defects but minimal fundus abnormalities to avoid misdiagnosis as optic neuritis or other disorders. In patients with high myopia, myopia-related structural and functional alterations may influence the interpretation of ancillary examinations; therefore, comprehensive evaluation based on multimodal imaging and electrophysiological assessments is essential.

papers.title: A Curcumin-Based Polyherbal Slow-Dissolving Buccal Lozenge (CBFP-ODS) and Changes in Gingival Inflammation, Plaque Accumulation, Bleeding on Probing and Oral Malodour: A 12-Week Prospective Single-Arm Interventional Study in Young Adults.
papers.authors: Kumar V, Dedova LN, Sah N, Doctor NK, Kamble M
papers.abstract:
Plaque-induced gingivitis is the most prevalent reversible inflammatory condition of the gingival tissues and remains under-managed at the population level. Chlorhexidine, the most extensively studied chemical adjunct, is limited in sustained daily use by staining, taste alteration and mucosal effects, which motivates interest in botanically based oral wellness adjuncts intended for everyday use. This study was an uncontrolled, exploratory, hypothesis-generating evaluation of one such adjunct.
We evaluated a curcumin-based functional phytotherapeutic oral delivery system (CBFP-ODS), a sugar-free, slow-dissolving buccal lozenge containing six standardised botanicals (Curcuma longa, Ocimum sanctum, Zingiber officinale, Cinnamomum verum, Mentha piperita and Piper longum), in adults aged 18-35 years with mild-to-moderate gingivitis. In a prospective, single-arm, open-label, pre- and post-interventional study (120 enrolled), participants used one lozenge twice daily for 12 weeks while continuing routine mechanical plaque control. Outcomes at five timepoints (baseline, 1 week, 21 days, 45 days, 12 weeks) included the modified gingival index (MGI; primary outcome), the Silness and Löe Plaque Index (PI), the Ainamo and Bay Bleeding on Probing (BOP) index, an examiner-rated organoleptic score, an adapted breath-related self-perception (BRSP) scale and a WHO-adapted oral hygiene and behaviour composite. The pre-specified primary analysis was a completer analysis of the 115 participants with complete follow-up; a mixed-effects model on all 120 enrolled participants was the sensitivity analysis.
In the primary completer analysis (n = 115), MGI decreased from 1.78 (SD 0.41) to 0.96 (SD 0.36) (mean change 0.82, 95% CI: 0.73-0.91; t (114) = 18.9; p < 0.001; Cohen's dz ~1.76). Plaque, BOP, oral malodour and self-perceived breath showed within-subject reductions of ~43%-53%, and the behavioural composite increased by ~31% (all p < 0.001). The mixed-effects sensitivity analysis on all 120 enrolled participants gave a concordant estimated reduction of 0.81 MGI units (95% CI: 0.73-0.89). No product-related adverse events were recorded.
In this single-arm study, twice-daily use of CBFP-ODS was associated with within-subject improvements in gingival, plaque, bleeding and breath-related outcomes over 12 weeks. Because the design was uncontrolled and open-label, these observations cannot separate the effect of the intervention from improved oral hygiene behaviour, participation effects, regression to the mean or natural clinical variation and are hypothesis-generating. They do not demonstrate efficacy or verify mucosal absorption. Randomised, placebo-controlled and active-controlled trials are required before any statement about efficacy can be made. Trial Registration: Clinical Trials Registry, India: (CTRI/2025/06/088964; prospectively registered).

papers.title: Determinants of MoCA improvement in post-ischemic stroke patients receiving acupuncture: a retrospective study.
papers.authors: Long H, Wu P
papers.abstract:
Acupuncture is commonly integrated into multimodal rehabilitation programs for post-ischemic stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI), but the factors associated with cognitive improvement in this complex treatment context remain unclear. This retrospective study investigated factors associated with cognitive improvement in stroke patients receiving acupuncture as part of a standardized multimodal inpatient rehabilitation program.
In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 226 ischemic stroke patients treated with acupuncture between January 2023 and December 2025 were enrolled. Demographic data, clinical characteristics, acupuncture treatment parameters, and laboratory indicators were collected from electronic medical records. Cognitive function was assessed using MoCA, MMSE, LOTCA, MBI, HAMD, HAMA, and PSQI scales. Patients were categorized into improvement (ΔMoCA ≥2) and non-improvement groups. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were used to identify factors associated with cognitive improvement.
Among the 226 patients, 148 (65.49%) achieved improvement. After treatment, the improvement group showed significant improvements in MoCA and MMSE scores compared with baseline and the non-improvement group [between-group difference for post-treatment MoCA: 1.59 (95% CI 0.82 to 2.36; p < 0.001); MMSE: 2.44 (95% CI 1.69 to 3.19; p < 0.001)]. Significant improvements were also observed in LOTCA, MBI, HAMD, HAMA, and PSQI scores in the improvement group (p < 0.001). Univariate analysis identified age, education years, admission NIHSS score, diabetes mellitus, time to acupuncture intervention, treatment frequency, and total treatment course as factors associated with recovery (p < 0.05). Multivariate analysis demonstrated that advanced age (OR = 1.208, p < 0.001), higher NIHSS score (OR = 1.643, p = 0.001), longer time from stroke onset to acupuncture intervention (OR = 1.162, p = 0.011) and diabetes mellitus (OR = 4.737, p = 0.018) were associated with a lower probability of achieving the ΔMoCA improvement threshold. In contrast, longer education duration (OR = 0.740, p = 0.006), higher treatment frequency (OR = 0.271, p < 0.001), and longer treatment course (OR = 0.248, p < 0.001) were associated with a higher probability of meeting the improvement threshold. However, as treatment frequency and total course were determined during the clinical course rather than at baseline, these associations should be interpreted as exploratory and hypothesis-generating, and do not imply causality.
In this retrospective cohort of PSCI patients receiving acupuncture within a multimodal inpatient rehabilitation setting, shorter time from stroke onset to acupuncture initiation, higher weekly frequency, and longer treatment duration were exploratory factors associated with a greater likelihood of meeting the predefined ΔMoCA improvement threshold in this cohort. These hypothesis-generating observations may inform the design of future prospective studies and suggest patient characteristics that warrant further investigation. However, given the uncontrolled design, these findings cannot establish acupuncture-specific efficacy and should be considered hypothesis-generating, warranting confirmation through prospective randomized controlled trials.

papers.title: Lactobacillus-Based Therapy for Ulcerative Colitis: From Strain Heterogeneity and TCM-Mediated Modulation to Engineered Delivery and Precision Translation.
papers.authors: Zhang T, Lei H, Zhao X, Wang H, Chen X, Zhai Y et al.
papers.abstract: Although Lactobacillus sensu lato is widely considered a promising microecological intervention for ulcerative colitis, its clinical translation remains severely constrained by strain-specific efficacy, host microenvironmental dependency, and the risk of opportunistic systemic translocation across a compromised intestinal barrier. The historical assumption of genus-level therapeutic uniformity is increasingly inadequate, as even closely related strains can exhibit divergent or occasionally adverse clinical outcomes. This functional heterogeneity is rooted in distinct genomic architectures encoding carbohydrate-active enzymes, bile salt hydrolases, and surface adhesins, which collectively govern the metabolic and colonization behavior of live biotherapeutics. Furthermore, selectively expanding target strains within a competitive, exclusionary gut microbiota represents a major clinical bottleneck. To address these barriers, this review synthesizes the common protective networks of lactobacilli and the taxonomic heterogeneity that defines their efficacy and safety boundaries. We review how traditional Chinese medicine constituents may selectively modulate target strains through the potential substrate-enzyme compatibility and summarize advanced bioengineering platforms, including postbiotics (inactivated-cell preparations) and cell-free effector components, and responsive biomaterials, designed to protect these metabolic pathways. By deconstructing the molecular logic of functional divergence and pharmacological targeting, we argue that a promising direction for precision microecological therapy may involve moving beyond broad taxonomic classification toward quantitative matching of strain-specific functional and enzymatic fingerprints. This paradigm shift demands rigorous causal validation, context-responsive delivery systems, and a regulatory transition toward quality control standards incorporating biochemical effector activity units alongside, rather than instead of, viable-cell enumeration.

papers.title: Chinese herbal medicine formulas for Alzheimer's disease: Evidence, mechanisms, and translational standards.
papers.authors: Liang EX, Li QW, Liang H
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is defined biologically by amyloid and tau pathology. The emergence of biomarker-based diagnostic criteria, blood-based assays, and anti-amyloid therapeutic trials has substantially raised the evidentiary standard for all candidate AD interventions, including Chinese herbal medicine (CHM) formulas. However, CHM formula evidence for AD lacks critical appraisal and methodological standards. Thus, this review aims to: (1) critically evaluate the clinical, mechanistic, and translational evidence for oral or topical CHM formulas used in AD, specifically those selected according to Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) diagnostic; and (2) assess the methodological requirements necessary for credible development of such formulas in AD research. Preclinical studies suggest plausible effects of CHM formulas on amyloid-related pathways, tau phosphorylation, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and energy metabolism, but these findings remain hypothesis-generating rather than clinically validated. Most included studies relied on clinical diagnoses, likely encompassing mixed pathologies (e.g., vascular dementia, dementia with Lewy bodies, or depression-related cognitive impairment), rendering their results preliminary rather than confirmatory for biologically defined AD. Current evidence does not support CHM formulas as established therapies for AD. Future studies will require biomarker-confirmed diagnosis, rigorous formula quality control, prespecified TCM pattern stratification, clinically meaningful cognitive and functional endpoints, mechanistic target-engagement measures, and prospective safety and herb-drug interaction monitoring.

papers.title: SPIRIT-A: An Extension of SPIRIT 2025 for Acupuncture Clinical Trial Protocols.
papers.authors: Duan Y, Lin H, Zhou Z, Lee MS, Alraek T, Chan AW et al.
papers.abstract:
Protocols for acupuncture randomized controlled trials (RCTs) often lack adequate reporting of acupuncture-specific features. This study developed the Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials-Acupuncture (SPIRIT-A) extension to provide tailored reporting guidance for acupuncture clinical trial protocols.
The study followed EQUATOR Network guidance for developing health research reporting guidelines. A Development Group, Advisory Group, and international Delphi expert panel were established. The initial checklist was informed by two reviews assessing reporting quality using SPIRIT and Standard Protocol Items for Clinical Trials with Traditional Chinese Medicine (SPIRIT-TCM) extension respectively, and refined with reference to SPIRIT 2025, STandards for Reporting Interventions in Controlled Trials of Acupuncture (STRICTA), and the SPIRIT-TCM extension. A modified Delphi survey was conducted according to a predefined consensus criterion (≥80% agreement), followed by final expert endorsement.
Thirty-four experts from 10 countries participated in the Delphi survey, and all candidate items reached the predefined consensus threshold. The final checklist includes 34 items (57 subitems) that supplement SPIRIT 2025 with acupuncture-specific recommendations covering syndrome differentiation and treatment, procedural details, blinding and control design, acupuncturist qualifications, and safety monitoring.
SPIRIT-A provides structured reporting recommendations addressing key methodological considerations in acupuncture clinical trial protocols. Its development followed internationally recognized methodological standards and is expected to enhance the completeness and reproducibility of acupuncture RCT protocols and facilitate their broader dissemination and use.

papers.title: Research Progress of Astragali Complanati Semen Based on Bibliometric Analysis: Herbal Textual Research, Processing, Chemical Constituents, and Pharmacological Activities.
papers.authors: Wu H, Li D, Yang H, Li Z, Wang J, Zhao H et al.
papers.abstract:
Astragali Complanati Semen (ACS), the dried mature seeds of Astragalus complanatus R. Br., is a traditional Chinese medicine with a long history of medicinal use. According to traditional Chinese medicinal records, ACS is traditionally used for tonifying the kidney and strengthening yang, consolidating essence and reducing urinary frequency, and nourishing the liver and improving visual function. Modern phytochemical and pharmacological studies have revealed that ACS contains various bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, triterpenoid saponins, amino acids, fatty acids, sterols, sesquiterpenoids, polysaccharides, and trace elements, which may contribute to its traditional therapeutic applications.
This review aimed to identify research trends and hotspots in ACS and to summarize its geo-authenticity, processing methods, chemical constituents, pharmacological activities, mechanisms, and future prospects.
Bibliometric visualization was performed using publications retrieved from the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang Data Knowledge Service Platform (Wanfang), VIP Chinese Science and Technology Journal Database (VIP), Web of Science (WoS), and PubMed. The findings were integrated with a comprehensive review of herbal textual research, processing, chemical constituents, pharmacological effects, and mechanisms.
The number of publications increased steadily, with China accounting for the largest share. Institutions from 28 Chinese provinces and municipalities contributed, with Shaanxi Province showing the highest publication frequency. Research hotspots included geo-authenticity, processing, chemical constituents, pharmacological activities, and mechanisms. ACS contains diverse chemical constituents, including flavonoids, sesquiterpenoids, triterpenoid saponins, polysaccharides, and other constituents. Major pharmacological activities include antihypertensive, lipid-lowering, hepatoprotective, antifibrotic, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory effects.
This review clarifies ACS research trends and hotspots and comprehensively summarizes its major research domains. Future studies should focus on quality markers (Q-markers), the activities and mechanisms of flavonoid monomers, and the isolation, purification, structural characterization, and structure-activity relationships of polysaccharides.

papers.title: HaloTag-directed magnetic immobilization of PAD4 for target-based screening of natural-product inhibitors.
papers.authors: Xu H, Zhu D, Zhao Z, Zuo H, Wang Y, Fang Y et al.
papers.abstract: Target-directed screening of bioactive natural products is often limited by the instability, poor recoverability, and repeated preparation requirements of soluble recombinant enzymes. Here, we developed a reusable magnetic peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4) screening platform based on site-directed HaloTag immobilization. Recombinant Halo-PAD4 was captured directly from crude lysate by chloroalkane-functionalized magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs-Cl) without an additional labor-intensive and time-consuming enzyme purification step, generating MNPs-Halo-PAD4 with retained catalytic activity and inhibitor responsiveness. Compared with soluble PAD4, the immobilized enzyme showed improved activity retention during storage and temperature exposure and could be magnetically recovered for repeated assays. The platform was applied to screen water, 75% ethanol, and ethyl acetate extracts of 15 traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) materials. Among the tested materials, Alpinia officinarum consistently exhibited the strongest PAD4-inhibitory activity in both soluble and immobilized PAD4 assays. Activity-guided high-performance liquid chromatography fractionation localized the inhibitory activity to fraction F3. Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry tentatively annotated 13 constituents, and authentic-standard testing prioritized galangin. Galangin inhibited PAD4 with an IC50 value of 46.6 μM and showed direct interaction with PAD4 by biolayer interferometry, with an apparent KD of 7.8 μM. Molecular docking further provided a structural hypothesis for the interaction. This workflow combines HaloTag-chloroalkane chemistry, magnetic enzyme immobilization, liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry for the screening of PAD4 inhibitors. This proposed one-step capture and immobilization of recombinant protein also supports ligand screening for other protein targets.
