papers.title: Comparative Efficacy of Different Moxibustion Therapies on Pain and Functional Improvement in Knee Osteoarthritis: A Network Meta-Analysis.
papers.authors: Wang M, Ye Y, Cheng Y, Pan L, Chen Y
papers.abstract:
This network meta-analysis aimed to systematically compare the efficacy of various moxibustion therapies in alleviating pain, improving joint function, and increasing the overall response rate in patients with knee osteoarthritis (KOA). Additionally, this study explored potential sources of heterogeneity to provide evidence-based support for clinical decision-making.
We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and SinoMed from inception to March 30, 2026, for RCTs evaluating moxibustion modalities for KOA. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using ROB 2.0. Network meta-analysis was conducted in Stata 17.0 using a frequentist framework. Effects were expressed as SMDs or RRs with 95% CIs, and treatments were ranked by SUCRA. Heterogeneity, inconsistency, and evidence certainty were assessed using Cochran's Q test, node-splitting analysis, and CINeMA, respectively.
For pain (23 RCTs, 1,740 participants), heat-sensitive moxibustion was the only intervention significantly better than usual care (SMD -2.27, 95% CI -4.47 to -0.07; SUCRA 83.9%). For joint function (17 RCTs, 1,459 participants), heat-sensitive and conventional moxibustion were both significant, with heat-sensitive moxibustion ranking highest (SUCRA 78%). For overall response rate (8 trials, 702 participants), conventional moxibustion was superior to usual care (RR 1.35, 95% CI 1.08-1.80; SUCRA 97.3%). Certainty of evidence was low to very low.
Evidence of low to very low certainty indicates that heat-sensitive moxibustion may improve pain and joint function compared with usual care, while conventional moxibustion may increase the overall response rate. However, no moxibustion modality demonstrated clear overall superiority over others. These findings warrant cautious interpretation. Larger, multicentre RCTs with standardized protocols and robust blinding are needed to clarify comparative effectiveness.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture for Procedural Anesthesia: A Scoping Review of Stimulation Parameters and Anesthetic-Sparing Outcomes.
papers.authors: Lee C, Chu H, Kim K, Park S, Kang K, Kim S et al.
papers.abstract:
Pharmacological local anesthetics carry risks of systemic toxicity and hypersensitivity and do not attenuate the surgical stress response. Electroacupuncture (EA) has been proposed as an adjunct for procedural anesthesia, but the heterogeneous clinical evidence has not been systematically mapped.
This scoping review was registered on the Open Science Framework and follows PRISMA-ScR. PubMed/MEDLINE, CENTRAL, Web of Science, CNKI and J-STAGE were searched from inception to April 8, 2026, without language restrictions. Eligible human studies used needle-based EA, alone or with pharmacological anesthesia, for procedural local or regional anesthesia, nerve block or local anesthetic dose reduction. Consistent with scoping review methodology, no formal critical appraisal or risk-of-bias assessment was undertaken.
Thirty-nine studies published between 1971 and 2025 were included: randomized controlled trials (59%), non-randomized and observational studies (36%) and case reports (5%), spanning minor soft-tissue, head and neck, anorectal and abdominal, and spinal and orthopedic procedures, mixed surgical series and experimental pain models. Of the 20 studies that quantified local anesthetic consumption, seven allowed calculation of reductions relative to controls (10%-86%), which were calculated on different dose bases and are not directly comparable. A small number of studies reported no requirement for supplemental local anesthetic or rescue medication. The dense-disperse 2/100 Hz waveform with a 20-30-minute pre-operative induction phase was the most frequently used protocol in trials published from 2012 onward.
This review maps potentially promising stimulation parameters but cannot establish the efficacy or clinical superiority of EA. The 2/100 Hz protocol with structured pre-operative induction should be regarded as a hypothesis-generating starting point for standardized trials, for which this evidence map provides a design framework. Kilohertz-frequency stimulation, studied only experimentally, is a hypothesis for future research.
Open Science Framework, DOI: https://osf.io/4n357 (registered April 28, 2026).
Clinical trial number: not applicable.

papers.title: Association of HTR3A and COMT polymorphisms with electroacupuncture response for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting in breast cancer: a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
papers.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
papers.authors: Zheng Y, Xiao W, Guan Y, Zhao F, Li J, Wang Z et al.
papers.abstract:
Preliminary findings indicate that electroacupuncture (EA) reduces chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV), yet individual responses vary. This study aimed to explore associations between selected single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and complete protection (CP) against CINV and to conduct an exploratory evaluation of their predictive value.
This exploratory analysis was based on a randomized controlled trial (RCT) of EA (NCT05275569). Three candidate SNPs in HTR3A and COMT were genotyped by Sanger sequencing. The primary outcome measure was CP against CINV, defined according to the endpoint of the prospective study. Firth logistic regression was applied to evaluate associations between clinical or genetic variables and CP under additive, dominant and recessive models.
A total of 189 patients with breast cancer (BC) were enrolled, with 96 allocated to true EA group and 93 to sham EA group. The two groups were comparable in clinical variables and genotype distribution, and all three SNPs conformed to Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium (HWE). In the true EA group, CP achievement rates varied by rs909411 genotype: 42.9% (AA), 32.1% (AG), and 62.3% (GG) (P = 0.027). Univariable Firth logistic regression indicated that rs909411 was associated with a higher likelihood of achieving CP under both additive (OR = 2.088, 95% CI: 1.089-4.249, P = 0.026) and recessive models (OR = 3.080, 95% CI: 1.327-7.429, P = 0.009). After Multivariable adjustment, rs909411 remained statistically significant (additive: OR = 2.138, P = 0.027; recessive: OR = 3.241, P = 0.011). rs4633 was associated with a lower likelihood of achieving CP under the recessive model (univariable OR = 0.089, P = 0.035; Multivariable OR = 0.059, P = 0.016). No consistent association was observed for rs4680, and no significant SNP-by-treatment interactions were detected.
Exploratory treatment-stratified analyses identified associations of rs909411 and rs4633 with CP within the true EA group.

papers.title: Entropy-driven DNA circuit coupled with Cas9 trans-cleavage for dual-amplified label-free electrochemical sensing of aflatoxin B1 and lead ions.
papers.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
papers.authors: Lei J, Chen F, Shi K
papers.abstract: Sensitive and reliable detection of hazardous contaminants in food and pharmaceutical products is important for public health and quality control. Herein, we developed ECG-Cas9 (Entropy-driven Circuit-assisted G-quadruplex Electrochemical Cas9 sensing) by coupling an entropy-driven DNA circuit (EDC) with Cas9 trans-cleavage and G-quadruplex-based electrochemical signal generation. Recognition of AFB1 or Pb2+ by the corresponding functional nucleic acids initiates the EDC and generates Cas9 activators. The activated Cas9 subsequently cleaves G-quadruplex-containing hairpin probes immobilized on the electrode surface, allowing the released G-quadruplex sequences to bind hemin and generate an enhanced electrochemical response. The combination of EDC amplification and Cas9 trans-cleavage provides dual signal amplification, achieving detection limits of 0.1 pg mL-1 for AFB1 and 0.5 pM for Pb2+. ECG-Cas9 also showed good selectivity toward both targets. Notably, the use of the G-quadruplex/hemin complex as the electrochemical signal reporter avoids additional electroactive labeling and simplifies probe preparation. Finally, the method was applied to the determination of AFB1 and Pb2+ in food and traditional Chinese medicine samples, with satisfactory analytical performance. These results suggest that ECG-Cas9 provides a sensitive and practical approach for contaminant analysis in complex samples.

papers.title: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis treated with the modified Bu-Shen-Jian-Pi decoction (mBSJP): Multicenter study.
papers.journal: International journal of clinical pharmacology and therapeutics
papers.authors: Han X, Li R, Zhang H, Liu Y, Loong SK, Wei S et al.
papers.abstract:
To investigate whether the modified Bu-Shen-Jian-Pi decoction (mBSJP) is more efficacious than the hitherto used and promoted BSJP formula in the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).
ALS is a fatal neurodegenerative disease with no satisfactory treatment option. Currently, there are few palliative care methods that can significantly delay the progression of the disease, and the efficacy of the herbal treatments used hitherto has also been unsatisfactory.
A total of 165 patients with ALS who met the diagnostic criteria after screening were randomly allocated into two groups, a modified Bu-Shen-Jian-Pi decoction group referred to as the mBSJP group and the placebo group. Clinical efficacy and side effects were evaluated during a 16-week observation period. Primary outcomes included Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Symptom Score in Integrative Treatment Scale (ALS-SSIT) and Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Rating Scale-Revised (ALSFRS-R) scores, and secondary observation parameters were 36-Item Short-Form Health Survey Questionnaire (SF-36) and forced vital capacity (FVC).
A total of 73 patients in the mBSJP group and 71 patients in the placebo group completed the trial. At the end of the 16th week of treatment, there were significant statistical differences observed between the two groups in values for both the ALS-SSIT and the ALSFRS-R scores showing that mBSJP significantly delayed progression of the disease and appearance of symptoms compared to the administration of placebo.
Treatment of ALS with mBSJP delays disease progression and is recommended as a treatment option for ALS in regions where the use of traditional Chinese medicine is regulated and approved.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture relieves neuropathic pain via modulation of the ferroptosis pathway through GPX4.
papers.journal: Acupuncture in medicine : journal of the British Medical Acupuncture Society
papers.authors: Wen X, Huang A, Kui W, Li Y, Gu Z, Xie L et al.
papers.abstract:
Neuropathic pain (NP) is a chronic condition with complex mechanisms and limited treatments. While electroacupuncture (EA) shows promising analgesic effects, its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated whether EA modulates ferroptosis to alleviate NP via glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4).
A chronic constriction injury (CCI) rat model was employed. EA was administered at ST36 and GB34 for 14 consecutive days. Pain hypersensitivity, neuronal injury, glial activation, ferroptosis-related markers, mitochondrial morphology and the effect of co-administration of Ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1) were assessed.
EA alleviated CCI-induced pain hypersensitivity, restoring mechanical withdrawal threshold (MWT) to 77.2% and paw withdrawal latency (PWL) to 85.4% of sham group levels (p < 0.01). Immunofluorescence analysis revealed that EA increased neuronal nuclei (NeuN)-positive cell counts by 41.5% (p < 0.001) while reducing glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule (Iba)-1 expression by 48.2% and 54.7%, respectively (p < 0.001). EA restored GPX4 expression (2.3-fold, p < 0.01), increased glutathione (GSH) levels, and reduced acyl-coenzyme A (CoA) synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4), malondialdehyde (MDA) and iron accumulation. Furthermore, EA reversed mitochondrial shrinkage and cristae disruption. Immunofluorescence confirmed increased GPX4 co-localization in spinal neurons. Notably, co-administration with Fer-1 further enhanced neuroprotection and pain relief, suggesting additive effects.
These findings suggest that EA relieves NP by modulating GPX4-mediated ferroptosis, inhibiting lipid peroxidation and preserving mitochondrial integrity. The enhanced effect with EA and Fer-1 in combination further supports ferroptosis modulation as a potential mechanism underlying EA-induced analgesia.

papers.title: Early Acupuncture Following Thrombolysis in Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials on Efficacy and Safety.
papers.authors: Li G, Zhou Y, He Z, Li S, Bai Q, Fan S et al.
papers.abstract:
Intravenous thrombolysis is standard for acute ischemic stroke (AIS), but many patients still have poor outcomes. Acupuncture may confer additional neuroprotection, yet its safety and efficacy when initiated early post-thrombolysis remain unclear.
A systematic search of databases and registries was conducted from inception to March 31, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing thrombolysis plus acupuncture with thrombolysis plus conventional post-thrombolytic care in AIS patients within 14 days of onset. Meta-analyses were performed using mean differences (MD) or risk ratios (RR) with 95% CIs. Heterogeneity was assessed with the I2 statistic; publication bias was evaluated via Egger's test. Pre-specified subgroup analyses were conducted.
Ten trials (1116 patients) were included. Adjunctive acupuncture reduced neurological deficit (NIHSS MD -2.90, 95% CI -3.62 to -2.17), improved activities of daily living (Barthel Index MD 12.07, 95% CI 8.10-16.03), and increased clinical response (RR 1.16, 95% CI 1.11-1.21; all p < 0.001). Adverse events did not differ significantly (RR 0.52, 95% CI 0.25-1.08). Only one study reported symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (zero acupuncture vs. six control). Benefits were consistent across subgroups.
In AIS patients receiving thrombolysis, acupuncture initiated early following thrombolysis improves neurological and functional outcomes. In available safety data, adverse events did not differ significantly between groups; however, systematic surveillance for symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage was lacking in most trials. These findings support further rigorous evaluation of early post-thrombolysis acupuncture in adequately monitored randomized trials.

papers.title: Scoping Review of Acupuncture for Migraine: Current Evidence and Research Gaps.
papers.authors: Wu Y, Ji Y, Wu Y, Li W, Zhang J, Yao C et al.
papers.abstract:
Migraine is a disabling neurological disorder that significantly impairs quality of life and imposes a substantial socioeconomic burden. While acupuncture has shown clinical benefits for migraine management, the scope and methodological quality of the existing evidence remain unclear. This scoping review aimed to map the current landscape of clinical research on acupuncture for migraine, characterize the evidence base, identify research gaps, and inform future research priorities.
We systematically searched CNKI, WanFang, SinoMed, PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science from inception to January 13, 2026. A total of 269 randomized controlled trials were included.
Most studies originated from China, with limited English-language publications. Migraine without aura was the most frequently investigated subtype, and the ICHD criteria were commonly applied. The most frequently used acupoints were GB20, GB8, and LR3, while the GB and TE meridians were selected most often. The most common body region combination targeted the head (caput) and neck (collum). Conventional acupuncture was the predominant technique, followed by electroacupuncture and blood-letting therapy. Outcome measures fell into four categories: objective headache parameters, assessment scales, efficacy and safety indicators, and mechanistic or adjunctive measures. Despite the breadth of studies, reporting quality was limited: only 1.49% of trials enrolled more than 300 participants and 43.12% did not report follow-up duration. Methodological limitations also included inadequate randomization reporting, insufficient blinding, and heterogeneity in core outcome definitions. These inconsistencies limit cross-study comparability and evidence synthesis.
Future research should prioritize rigorous methodology, standardized protocols, and candidate outcome domains to guide future consensus development, enhancing the validity and clinical applicability of acupuncture research for migraine.

papers.title: Efficacy, safety and mechanism of Jinfeng pill in the treatment of perimenopausal syndrome: A protocol for a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial.
papers.authors: Wu X, Zhou L, Hu J, Tian M, Liu S, Song K et al.
papers.abstract:
Perimenopausal syndrome (PMPS) refers to a series of physiological and psychological symptoms caused by the fluctuation or decline of sex hormone levels during the pre- and postmenopausal periods. With the acceleration of aging society, more and more women suffer from symptoms of PMPS. Jinfeng Pill (JFP) is a classic Chinese patent medicine for gynecological diseases, but it lacks rigorous clinical evidence for the treatment of PMPS.
This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial will be conducted across three hospitals in China. A total of 100 perimenopausal women will be randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive JFP or placebo for 12 weeks, followed by a 4-week post-treatment follow-up. The primary outcome is the modified Kupperman Index (KI), assessed at baseline and at weeks 4, 8, 12, and 16. Secondary outcomes include the Hot Flash scale (HFs), the Menopause-Specific Quality of Life (MENQOL) questionnaire, the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD), the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA), the Vaginal Health Index Score (VHIS), and Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) symptom score. Mechanistic outcomes encompass serum sex hormones and estrogen metabolites, inflammatory cytokines interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), gut microbiota composition (16S rRNA sequencing), faecal β-glucuronidase (β-GUS) activity, and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) concentrations.
This is the first multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to investigate the molecular mechanism by which JFP ameliorate PMPS by reshaping the gut microbiota structure, modulating β-GUS activity, optimizing SCFAs metabolism, suppressing inflammatory responses, and maintaining estrogen homeostasis. The results of this trial will help us to evaluate the efficacy, safety and possible mechanism of JFP in treating PMPS.
The protocol (Version 3.0, dated November 19, 2025) was approved by the Ethics Committee of Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology (approval number: TJ-IRB202512083). Written informed consent will be obtained from all participants prior to enrolment. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and academic conference presentations.

papers.title: Thymidine mitigates LPS-induced acute lung injury by regulating gut microbiota and metabolism through the lung-gut axis.
papers.authors: Luo M, Zeng M, Zhang Y, Guo P, Zhang Z, Wu Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Yam (Dioscorea opposita Thunb.) is a prominent traditional Chinese medicine with the core function of tonifying the lungs. Thymidine (Thy), a compound extracted from the stems and leaves of yam, has an unclear mechanism of action on acute lung injury (ALI).
An ALI model was established by tracheal infusion LPS. Pulmonary edema, lung histopathology, lung function, oxidative stress, immunity, and inflammation of mice were detected. The analysis of metabolomics, intestinal flora, and lung PPAR-γ levels was to clarify the mechanism of Thy on ALI. The co-culture of Beas-2B and Caco-2 was used to investigate the effects of Thy combined with the PPAR-γ agonist rosiglitazone and antagonist T0070907 on the levels of PPAR-γ, oxidative stress, inflammation, and metabolites in LPS-induced cell model.
Thy improved pulmonary edema and pathological damage in the lungs, reduced oxidative stress and immune inflammatory levels, and affected the balance of intestinal microbiota in ALI mice, as well as arachidonic acid metabolism, and regulated the levels of PPAR-γ. Under co-culture, Thy reduced oxidative stress levels in Beas-2B and Caco-2 and alleviated the levels of PPAR-γ, inflammatory factors, and metabolites in Beas-2B. And the effect of Thy was blocked by T0070907, and rosiglitazone promoted the role of Thy.
Thy may ameliorate intestinal dysbiosis and metabolic disorders via the lung-gut axis and regulate the levels of PPAR-γ to mitigate LPS-induced ALI.

papers.title: Acupuncture for healthy-ageing-relevant outcomes in older cancer survivors: a scoping review with implications for future research and practice.
papers.journal: Journal of cancer survivorship : research and practice
papers.authors: Lam CS, Li X, Wu HV, Zhu L, Chow V, Chimonas S et al.
papers.abstract:
Older cancer survivors face multidimensional challenges to healthy ageing and independence. Acupuncture has growing evidence for pain and symptom management, but its role in promoting healthy ageing remains unclear. This scoping review mapped evidence across four healthy-ageing-relevant domains, including physical function, psychological distress, cognition, and medication use, and identified knowledge gaps.
We searched PubMed, Embase, and Scopus from inception through June 30, 2026. Eligible studies evaluated acupuncture among adult cancer survivors; studies restricted to younger populations were excluded. Findings were extracted and narratively synthesized across the four domains.
Of 986 records identified, 39 articles representing 37 studies were included. Most were randomized controlled trials (n = 21, 56.8%), and breast cancer was the most frequently studied (n = 22, 59.5%). Most studies assessed healthy-ageing-relevant outcomes as secondary outcomes in symptom-focused studies, with pain being the most common primary outcome (n = 9, 24.3%). No study specifically targeted older cancer survivors (age 65 or older). Physical function (n = 28, 75.7%) and psychological distress (n = 17, 45.9%) were the most frequently studied domains, whereas cognition (n = 8, 21.6%) and medication use (n = 10, 27.0%) were less frequently evaluated. Acupuncture showed promising improvements in functional outcomes and anxiety/depression compared with usual care or waitlist, whereas findings were more mixed with sham or active comparators and other outcomes.
Acupuncture is promising to support healthy ageing related outcomes among cancer survivors; however, rigorous controlled clinical trials focusing on older adults are lacking. Future prospective trials focusing on addressing these important and novel outcomes will inform evidence-based integration of acupuncture for older adults impacted by cancer.
Acupuncture may complement survivorship care to support healthy ageing, particularly by addressing functional limitations and psychological distress.

papers.title: Signal-amplified fluorescent biosensing for exosomes analysis and exosomes-driven high-throughput screening of traditional Chinese medicine.
papers.authors: Zhang Q, Huang F, Duan H, Liu Q, Wang H, Wang W et al.
papers.abstract: Exosomes, extracellular vesicles involved in intercellular communication and disease progression, have emerged as promising therapeutic targets and drug delivery vehicles. Targeting exosomes for drug screening offers significant potential in developing treatments for cancer. However, conventional methods for exosome-based drug discovery often lack sensitivity, specificity. To address these limitations, we propose a signal-amplified fluorescent biosensing (SAFB) system designed to screen drugs by specifically targeting exosomal biomarkers. This sensor integrates exosome-specific surface markers (Epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM)) with dual fluorescence amplification cascade probes (catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA), CdTe quantum dots (QDs)), enabling highly sensitive, label-free detection of exosomes and exosome-drug interactions. Moreover, SAFB is employed for high-throughput screening (HTS) to identify active compounds from Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM). HFB-5D is screened out by inhibiting the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway to inhibit breast cancer growth. Overall, this work provides a versatile and promising tool for exosomes analysis and advancing exosome-related drug discovery.

papers.title: The Effectiveness of Non-surgical Interventions for Managing Chronic Low Back Pain.
papers.authors: Elanchezhian K, Devaraj K, Saravanan S, Raj BKS, Ravella V
papers.abstract:
Chronic low back pain (CLBP) is a widespread condition with a substantial effect on quality of life and work capacity. Non-drug, non-surgical options - physical therapy (PT), cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), and acupuncture - appear promising, yet stronger empirical evidence is still needed to confirm their value.
This study set out to compare PT, CBT, and acupuncture against standard care for the management of CLBP.
Two hundred participants with a diagnosis of CLBP took part in a randomized controlled trial and were allocated to one of four arms - PT, CBT, acupuncture, or standard-care control. Pain intensity, functional disability, quality of life, and psychological well-being were recorded at baseline and again at 6 and 12 weeks, using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), 36-item short form survey (SF-36), and beck depression inventory (BDI), respectively; outcomes were compared using analysis of variance with post hoc testing.
All three active arms outperformed the control. Both PT and acupuncture produced marked reductions in pain (VAS) and disability (ODI) scores (P < 0.01), whereas CBT produced its largest gains in psychological well-being (BDI) (P < 0.01) alongside more modest gains in pain and disability. SF-36 scores rose across every domain in the treatment arms, with PT and acupuncture producing the strongest gains in the physical-functioning and pain domains (P < 0.01).
PT, CBT, and acupuncture each represent a viable non-surgical option for CLBP, delivering meaningful gains in pain, function, and psychological well-being. Incorporating them into routine care could support a more holistic model of CLBP management, improving outcomes while lowering dependence on drug-based treatment.

papers.title: Non Pharmacological Pain Management in Sickle Cell Disease, a Narrative Review.
papers.authors: Daudi K, Bashir J, Aja L
papers.abstract:
Pain is a major cause of morbidity, disability, and reduced quality of life among people living with sickle cell disease (SCD). Although pharmacological treatment remains essential, non pharmacological interventions may provide complementary strategies for pain coping and symptom management. However, the strength of evidence supporting individual interventions varies considerably.
This narrative review aimed to critically evaluate the evidence for non pharmacological interventions used to manage acute and chronic pain in SCD, distinguish disease-specific findings from indirect evidence, identify limitations in the literature, and discuss implications for clinical practice and resource-constrained settings.
The review examined randomized controlled trials, quasi-experimental studies, observational studies, systematic reviews, and clinical practice guidelines addressing non pharmacological pain management in SCD. The evidence covered psychological and behavioral interventions, physical and sensory approaches, technology-assisted interventions, and supportive coping practices. Original SCD-specific studies were prioritized when evaluating intervention effectiveness. Findings from other chronic pain populations were treated as contextual evidence rather than proof of effectiveness in SCD.
The evidence was most developed for selected psychological and behavioral interventions, particularly cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and biofeedback in pediatric populations. In a multicenter randomized controlled trial involving adolescents with SCD, a digital CBT intervention was associated with a greater reduction in average pain intensity and fewer pain days at six months than an education control. Pediatric systematic reviews also identified studies investigating massage, virtual reality, yoga, and biofeedback; however, the evidence was limited by intervention heterogeneity, small sample sizes, methodological limitations, and inconsistent outcome reporting. The American Society of Hematology conditionally recommended massage, yoga, transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS), virtual reality, and guided audiovisual relaxation as adjuncts for acute SCD pain, based on very-low-certainty evidence. The available evidence for TENS was insufficient to establish benefit or harm. SCD-specific evidence for acupuncture, mindfulness-based interventions, hypnosis, and spiritual interventions was insufficient to establish their comparative analgesic effectiveness.
Non pharmacological interventions may complement pharmacological treatment and support pain coping in SCD, but their effectiveness should be evaluated individually rather than assumed across intervention categories. Clinical decisions should consider patient preferences, intervention-specific evidence, clinical circumstances, safety, and local resources. Larger controlled trials and implementation studies, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa and other low- and middle-income countries, are needed.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture Combined with Surround Needling for Acute Lateral Ankle Sprain in Adults: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Hu Q, Cai Q, Qi B, Cai J, Wang J, Liang Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Acute lateral ankle sprain (ALAS) has a high incidence in adults. Improper acute-stage intervention causes prolonged pain, swelling and impaired functional recovery. Conventional ice plus brake rest has limited rehabilitation efficacy. This study investigated the clinical efficacy and safety of electroacupuncture (EA) combined with surround needling for adult ALAS.
In this single-center randomized controlled trial, 95 patients aged 18-60 years with ALAS were 1:1:1 randomized to EA+surround needling (n=34), sham EA (n=32) or control (ice+brake rest, n=29) groups. Outcomes were the Kofoed score and musculoskeletal ultrasound, assessed at baseline and weeks 1, 2, 3 and 9. Adverse events were monitored throughout.
EA improved Kofoed scores more than control or sham EA from week 2 to week 9 (adjusted mean differences 7.8-11.4, 95% CI excluding zero). Kofoed AUC (baseline to week 9, points × week) was greater with EA (675.5, 95% CI 658.3-692.8). AUC differences were 39.51 vs control (95% CI 19.32-59.70) and 24.76 vs sham EA (95% CI 6.05-43.47). EA reduced anterior talofibular ligament thickness more than both groups and calcaneofibular ligament thickness more than control.
EA combined with surround needling was superior to sham EA and ice plus brake rest in improving ankle function assessed by the Kofoed score and reducing anterior talofibular ligament thickness, and superior to ice plus brake rest in reducing calcaneofibular ligament thickness. However, larger, longer-term trials are needed to verify these findings.
